title: Western Blotting
author: Cynthia L. Blanco

steps_raw.instruction: Protein Extraction and Western Blotting
Fill Beadbeater tubes (BioSpec Products, Inc., Oklahoma, USA) approximately ¼ full with 1mm diameter zirconia beads (BioSpec)
Add 20-25 mg of tissue and 400-500uL homogenizing buffer
Use the bead beater (Mini Beadbeater 16, BioSpec) to homogenize tissue samples for 1 to 2 minutes
Allow samples to rest on ice for 5-10 minutes after homogenization
Transfer homogenate to clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and centrifuge at 4°C for 10 minutes at 10,000xg
Remove the supernatant to clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. Discard pellet.
Quantify protein via spectrophotometric determination of absorbance at 280 nm (Epoch plate reader with Take3 microplate, BioTek, Vermont, USA)
Store protein samples at -80°C
Thaw protein samples on ice

Prepare western blotting cells to run gels (Mini Trans-Blot Cell; 10X tris/glycine/SDS running buffer, diluted to 1X in ddH20; Mini-PROTEAN TGX precast gels- 10% agarose; BioRad Laboratories, California, USA)
Fill volume to 15 uL with ddH20
Heat samples for 5 minutes at 95°C
Load samples, molecular weight marker, and controls into prepared gel
Stack gel for 30 minutes at 50 volts
Run gel for ~1 hour at 100-120 volts

Prepare cells for transfer (Mini Trans-Blot Cell with transfer accessories; 10X tris/glycine transfer buffer, diluted to 1X in ddH20 with 20% methanol; 0.4 micron nitrocellulose membranes; BioRad Laboratories)
Set up transfer and run for 1 hour at 100 volts. Entire transfer process is done at 4°C.
Block membranes in 10% milk/0.05%TWEEN in 1X TBS (BioRad Laboratories) for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle rocking
Probe membranes with primary antibody (diluted in 3% milk/0.05% TWEEN in 1X TBS) overnight at 4°C, with gentle rocking.
Pour off primary antibody and wash membranes in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS 3 times for 5 minutes each
Incubate membranes in secondary antibody (diluted in 5% milk/0.05% TWEEN in 1X TBS) for 1 hour at room temperature, with gentle rocking
Pour off secondary antibody and wash membranes in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS 3 times for 10 minutes each
Prepare 1:1 mixture of ECL reagents (Western Lighting Plus, Perkin Elmer, LLC, Massachusetts, USA)
Cover membranes with ECL for 1 minute
Gently dab edges of membranes on a napkin to removed excess moisture, place into radiography cassette
In a dark room, place radiography film (HyBlot CL, 8 x 10 inch, Denville Scientific, Massachusetts, USA) into radiography cassette and expose to membranes for 30 seconds to 2 minutes
Place films into X-ray developer (Mini-med/90 X-ray film processor, AFP imaging, Geogria, USA)
When finished developing, rinse excess ECL from membranes with ddH20
Place membranes into stripping buffer (Restore Plus Western Blot Stripping Buffer, Thermo-Fisher, USA) for 7 minutes
Rinse membranes in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS, then wash in 0.05% TWEEN/ 1X TBS for 2 ½ minutes
Block membrane as before and reprobe membrane for housekeeping gene (GAPDH)
Quantifying Western Blots
Place film on a clean sheet of white paper
Scan the film as a JPEG at high resolution, in black and white (HP Color LaserJet Pro MFP M477fdn, Hewlett-Packard, California, USA)
Open the image using imageJ (National Institutes of Health, Maryland, USA)
Use the rectangle tool to draw a box around the band to be quantified.
Press ctrl+1 to set the first row to be quantified.
Drag and drop, or use the arrow keys to move the box around to the next band to be quantified. Press ctrl+2 to set the next row. Repeat this step until all of the rows/bands have been selected.
After the final row, press ctrl+3 to create the plots of the rows
Use the line tool on ImageJ to draw a line across the bottom of each peak
Use the magic wand tool to quantify the area under the peak.
Copy and paste the numbers into an excel datasheet
Continue until you have measurements for all of your blots
These measurements represent the raw OD values of the blots.
Divide all of the OD values from your protein of interest by their corresponding value on the housekeeping gene reprobe.

When comparing two or more blots, normalize the gels to each other. Use the bands representing the internal control samples. Since these bands represent the same sample, they should be equal, so you’ll normalize the gel to reflect this:
Divide the internal control sample on gel A by the same internal control sample on gel B to get your correction value, C
Report the raw values of gel A, and multiply all of the values in gel B by C.
Continue this process until all of the gels you want to compare have been normalized
Calculate group means and standard deviations (or standard error) using the normalized data
Western Blotting Reagent Recipes
100mL running buffer concentrate (10 X Tris/Glycine/SDS [BioRad])
Mix gently in 1 liter bottle. Store at room temperature.
400mL Transfer Buffer Concentrate (10X Tris/Glycine Buffer [BioRad])
Add ingredients in that order. Mix gently in 4 liter bottle. Store in at 4°C
Mix gently in 1 liter bottle. Store short-term at room temperature, long-term at 4°C
Probing/Blocking buffers
To make a 3% solution: dissolve 1.5g non-fat dry milk in 50 mL TBS-Tween
To make a 5% solution: dissolve 2.5g non-fat dry milk in 50 mL TBS-Tween
To make a 10% solution: dissolve 5g non-fat dry milk in 50 mL TBS-Tween
Sample Loading Buffer (6X Laemmli Buffer)
18.75ml of 1.0M Tris (ph 6.8) **
Fill volume with ddH20 to 50ml
** If pH is greater than 6.8, adjust to 6.7 with HCl. If it is lower, do not use.
† 1% Bromophenol Blue: 0.1g BPB + 10ml H2O
Buffer A (AMPK Buffer)
Buffer B (Kei Buffer)
